title: Reconstruction of coherent formal-system morphisms from limit-sheaf maps
statement: Let Y be Noetherian, J a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf, and G,H coherent J-adic formal modules [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. For every O_Y-linear sheaf map β:lim G_n\to lim H_n, where both limits are in the category of module sheaves, there is a morphism α:G\to H of coherent formal modules whose induced limit map equals β. This is reconstruction for maps between limits of two coherent formal systems; there is no arbitrary pushforward system or proper morphism.

source.place: Lemma 087W and first half of Lemma 088B; checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/087W and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/088B

proof.text: Apply the ideal-power quotient identification to G and H at each level. Each limit projection is the cokernel projection followed by the supplied isomorphism, and is therefore epic.

For level n define a_n as e_G,n inverse, followed by formalModuleQuotientMap of beta at exponent n+1, followed by e_H,n. The existing quotient-map construction uses ideal-power multiplication naturality. Cokernel descent and the two projection equations give pi_G,n composed with a_n = beta composed with pi_H,n.

For every index morphism, precompose the desired naturality equation with the epic source limit projection. The two projection equations for a and the naturality equations of the limit cones identify the composites. Cancel the epimorphism to get a natural transformation. Package it as a morphism of the full subcategory. The limit-map projection equation and joint monicity of limit projections show that its induced map is beta.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 087W quotient formula; explicit categorical reconstruction from that formula (F2)

theorem coherentFormalModule_limit_full {Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian Y]
    (J : Y.IdealSheafData) (G H : CoherentFormalModule Y J)
    (β : limit G.obj ⟶ limit H.obj) :
    ∃ α : G ⟶ H, lim.map α.hom = β
